item.title: Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
item.description: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Swan, Maggie Haberman, Ana Swanson, Paul Mozur, Tripp Mickle and Julian E. Barnes
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, is influential at the White House on technology policy and has developed a close relationship with President Trump.

item.title: DoorDash to Buy Instacart for $17 Billion, Uniting 2 Delivery Giants
item.description: The deal combines the country’s largest restaurant delivery service with its biggest online grocery platform.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin and Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Amir Hamja/The New York Times
item.media:description: In its most recent quarter, DoorDash said it completed 970 million orders.

item.title: AI Is Finding a Flood of Bugs, and Silicon Valley Is Rushing to Fix Them
item.description: A.I. has uncovered a horde of software flaws, which engineers are racing to fix before they can be exploited and abused by hackers.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Ariel Davis

item.title: Hit the Road This Season With These Useful New Map Features
item.description: The recent updates to Google Maps and Apple’s Maps use artificial (and human) intelligence for better navigation, planning and travel guides.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:credit: Apple
item.media:description: The Flyover view in the latest version of Apple’s Maps app includes sharper aerial views of major cities so you can explore before you go.

item.title: Bodacious A.I. Bots Are Stealing Jokes From Young Female Comedians
item.description: Swiping jokes word for word, these bodacious bots mainly lift from young female comedians. What’s so insidious is how they’re subtly changing us, the audience.
item.dc:creator: Jason Zinoman

item.title: Alphabet’s Revenue Rises 25% as Profit Falls
item.description: The company has been spending relentlessly to build A.I. and said it would increase those investments next year. Profit dropped because of changes to the value of its investments.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Michael Hanson for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Google data center next to the Columbia River in The Dalles, Ore. “We’re excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us,” said Alphabet’s chief executive, Sundar Pichai.

item.title: Microsoft’s Profit Jumps 32% Despite Big Increase in Spending
item.description: The company’s free cash flow stayed positive in the last quarter even as it spent $45.2 billion on capital expenses like data centers and offered to pay workers to leave.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Grant Hindsley for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Redmond, Wash., campus of Microsoft, which reported $36.6 billion in profit for its latest quarter.

item.title: Apple Unveils Its First Touch-Screen MacBook Pro
item.description: Steve Jobs and Tim Cook both dismissed the idea, but Apple’s new chief executive is reimagining some of the company’s most important products.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang and Brian X. Chen
item.media:credit: David Fouts for The New York Times
item.media:description: The new Mac, with a starting price of $2,899, is the latest step into a new era for the consumer electronics giant.

item.title: GM Is Leaving NYSE for the Nasdaq After More Than 100 Years
item.description: After more than 100 years on the New York Stock Exchange, the automaker is shifting its listing to the Nasdaq, which is home to many technology companies.
item.dc:creator: Aruni Soni
item.media:credit: Brett Carlsen for The New York Times
item.media:description: At a General Motors factory in Tennessee.

item.title: The Key Numbers From Anthropic’s IPO Filing

item.dc:creator: Sri Muppidi and Lauren Hirsch
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic’s Code W/ Claude event in San Francisco in May. In a filing, the company provided rare insight into the business of a “frontier” A.I. lab that makes cutting-edge A.I. models.

item.title: Microsoft Offers Buyouts to 60,000 Employees as It Spends on A.I.
item.description: About a quarter of the tech giant’s employees were eligible for the packages, although the company cautioned it did not expect many employees to sign on.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO S-1 Spells Out a Future of Promise and Peril
item.description: The A.I. company took great pains to describe the many benefits that can come from using its Claude chatbot and technology, but also offered up a heavy dose of gloom.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac

item.title: Meet Anthropic’s Seven Founders as the A.I. Firm Prepares for an IPO
item.description: Former OpenAI employees started the company in 2021 after disagreements over how to safely build artificial intelligence. An I.P.O. could make them billionaires.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin

item.title: Anthropic S-1 Reveals Rapid Growth Ahead of Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Ahead of what could be the largest public listing ever, Anthropic said revenue soared to $16.3 billion in the first half of the year, and it planned to spend $807 billion on A.I. infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac, Erin Griffith, Lauren Hirsch and Sri Muppidi
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic, a powerhouse in A.I., is only five years old and seemingly came out of nowhere.

item.title: Darline Graham Gets Help From the Data Center Industry in South Carolina Senate Race
item.description: As political fights over artificial intelligence accelerate, there is now a super PAC aligned with the data center industry. Its first bet is on Ms. Graham, a Republican in an unexpectedly tight race.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer and Emily Davies
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford/Getty Images
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham of South Carolina has been friendlier toward the data center industry than her Democratic opponent, trying to walk a line between backing the centers’ development as a national security necessity while stressing the need for community involvement.

item.title: What’s Riding on Anthropic Going Public? Nearly Everything.
item.description: Anthropic sits atop a pyramid of business partners and suppliers, making it a barometer of the broader economy. Its initial public offering will have widespread implications.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith and Lauren Hirsch

item.title: Put Your A.I. Agents to Work with These 5 Killer Tasks

item.title: Elon Musk Says Ukraine Violated Starlink’s Rules

item.title: Why Anger About Data Centers and Energy Prices May Not Swing Votes
item.description: In Ohio, many voters say their frustration about the increase in electricity and fuel prices and the growth of data centers won’t influence whom they vote for.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott and Maddie McGarvey
item.media:description: In interviews, Ohio residents described data centers as threats to their communities. But many of them said the issue was not driving their choice for senator or governor.

item.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
item.description: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Gabriela Bhaskar/The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg. On Wednesday, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a record $25 billion penalty for abusing consumer privacy.
